prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1062; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a side impact at a controlled intersection and said the other vehicle entered from the left while the light was changing. The claim was opened and assigned for review the same day.

Entry 2: Verified the driver against the policy declarations and confirmed the named insured is listed as the operator of the vehicle involved. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone to take a full statement. The account of the approach, the impact point, and the sequence afterward matched the first report in every detail.

Entry 4: Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and lists the vehicles and their final rest positions. The responding officer recorded no citations at the time.

Entry 5: Received scene photos from the claimant showing the driver side door and rear quarter panel damage. The images confirm some of the details described but do not show the signal or the approach path.

Entry 6: Requested statements from nearby businesses and bystanders. No independent witnesses were located, and the claim will rely on the police report, photos, and the parties' accounts.

Entry 7: Obtained the repair estimate and inspected the vehicle. The pattern and location of the damage are consistent with the side impact described, and no prior damage to the same panels is recorded in the claim history.

Entry 8: Ran a prior claims and loss history search for the vehicle and the claimant. No earlier damage to this vehicle appears in any database checked.

Entry 9: The claimant reported neck pain and stiffness the day after the collision and was seen at urgent care. The reported injury is a neck strain, which fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type.

Entry 10: Medical records show treatment followed a usual course with physical therapy and home exercise. Symptoms improved steadily, and care tapered off as the claimant recovered. No earlier injury to the same area is known from the records obtained.

Entry 11: Reviewed the treatment bills and compared them with the injury and the expected recovery timeline. The charges are consistent with the care documented, and no unusual items were found.

Entry 12: Reviewed the file with the handling supervisor. The claim is supported by the policy, the vehicle damage, the police report, and the medical records, and it is ready for the settlement evaluation.
